# minimon-core (vendored)

The Pokémon Mini emulator core from [minimon.js](https://github.com/asterick/minimon.js)
(Bryon Vandiver, ISC license — see `LICENSE`), vendored here as the ground-truth S1C88
machine for the sdcc88 codegen test harness (`tests/emu/`).

Originally vendored from minimon.js commit `c3c3c9336111e1e0482a1138e583c686c3b1fb36`,
then **pruned to a minimal CPU + memory + interrupt harness** (the codegen tests need no
display/sound/peripherals):

- removed the LCD, blitter, and audio modules;
- removed the RTC, TIM256, GPIO, and EEPROM modules (the programmable **timers**
  are kept — they exercise interrupts);
- removed the **control** module (0x2000-0x2002 were three side-effect-free bytes nothing
  read back) and the **debug/`dprintf`** module (it only logged unhandled-register access).
  Those register accesses now follow plain open-bus behavior: an unhandled read returns the
  last bus value, an unhandled write is dropped;
- the **input (keypad) module is kept** — it is the deterministic interrupt source
  for the IRQ tests. Each keypad edge (K00-K07 → priority group 6, K10-K11 → group 5)
  raises its own maskable IRQ, and since the host drives the pad state on demand it
  can fire a chosen IRQ at a chosen instant — which is how `tests/emu/cases/12_nested_irq.c`
  preempts a running low-priority ISR with a higher-priority one. The guest requests a
  pad change through the runner's input mailbox (`emu_set_keys` → `update_inputs`);
- merged RAM + cartridge into one unified writable `memory[]` array, so far writes to
  ROM-space physical addresses stick and read back.

The CPU executes only off OSC3; the OSC1 (32 kHz) derivation is kept to clock the timers.

The embedded **BIOS was removed** (it couldn't boot with the peripherals gone, and the
runner already forces PC to the cartridge entry 0x2100 after reset). Low memory is now plain
writable RAM, so ISR tests can install interrupt vectors at 2*N (the table the CPU fetches
from on an interrupt). Everything outside the 0x2000..0x20FF register window is the unified
`memory[]`.

- `src/` — the emulator core (`*.cc`): CPU (`machine`/`operations`), IRQ, timers, input
- `include/` — its headers
- `table.h` — the opcode dispatch table. GENERATED by `tools/table.py` but checked
  in, pinned at this vendored version (`python3 tools/table.py > table.h` to refresh)
- `tools/` — `table.py` + `s1c88.csv`, the generator inputs for `table.h`

The core is plain C++17 with no dependencies; the host glue it expects
(`get_machine`) is provided by `tests/emu/runner.cc`.
